name: Kedarnath Dham
shortDesc: One of the most revered Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva surrounded by snow-clad peaks.
description: Kedarnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva nestled along the Mandakini river with majestic Himalayan snowy backdrops. Accessible by a scenic 16 km mountain trek from Gaurikund, it is one of the holiest shrines in India.

name: Badrinath Dham
shortDesc: Abode of Lord Vishnu located between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges.
description: Situated on the banks of the Alaknanda river, Badrinath is the most important of the four Char Dham pilgrimage destinations. Famous for its colorful facade and the sacred Tapt Kund hot springs.

name: Rishikesh
shortDesc: The Yoga Capital of the World and white-water river rafting hub on the Ganges.
description: Rishikesh balances ancient spiritual traditions with adrenaline-pumping extreme sports. Known for Triveni Ghat evening aarti, iconic suspension bridges, riverside camping, and meditation retreats.

name: Auli
shortDesc: India's premier skiing destination with 360-degree views of Nanda Devi.
description: Auli is renowned for its pristine alpine slopes, highest artificial lake, and one of the longest cable car ropeways in Asia connecting Joshimath to Auli. The panorama features Nanda Devi, Kamet, and Mana Parvat.

name: Chopta & Tungnath
shortDesc: Mini Switzerland of Uttarakhand and gateway to the highest Shiva temple in the world.
description: An unspoiled jewel of meadows and evergreen forest area in Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary. The trek ascends to Tungnath (3680m) and the dramatic Chandrashila peak summit (4000m).

name: Valley of Flowers
shortDesc: UNESCO World Heritage Site blossoming with over 500 varieties of exotic alpine wildflowers.
description: Discovered by Frank S. Smythe in 1931, this fairy-tale national park is blanketed in vivid blossoms during the monsoon. Home to rare Himalayan flora, blue sheep, and the snow leopard.

name: Nainital
shortDesc: The sparkling Lake District of India centered around pear-shaped Naini Lake.
description: Set in a valley containing an eye-shaped lake, Nainital is enveloped by seven emerald mountains. Boasting colonial heritage, Mall Road strolls, Naina Devi Temple, and panoramic snow views from Tiffin Top.

name: Mussoorie
shortDesc: Queen of the Hills offering dramatic views of the Doon Valley and Shivalik ranges.
description: Mussoorie has fascinated travelers since the British Raj. Home to cascading waterfalls, Gun Hill cable car, Lal Tibba observatory, and literary legacy celebrated by author Ruskin Bond.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
shortDesc: India's oldest national park and legendary sanctuary for the Royal Bengal Tiger.
description: Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, Corbett spans dense sal forests, the Ramganga river, and rolling grasslands. Renowned for jungle jeep safaris, wild elephants, and rich birdlife.

name: Munsiyari
shortDesc: Little Kashmir offering front-row views of the iconic Panchachuli five snow peaks.
description: Perched at the edge of the Tibetan border in eastern Kumaon, Munsiyari is the launchpad for Milam and Ralam Glacier expeditions. Famous for sunset glows over Panchachuli peaks and Shauka tribal culture.

name: Haridwar
shortDesc: Gateway to the Gods where River Ganga enters the Indo-Gangetic Plains.
description: One of India's seven holiest Hindu cities (Sapta Puri). Haridwar is celebrated for the magical Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri where thousands of floating diyas illuminate the sacred waters.

name: Kausani
shortDesc: Switzerland of India, dubbed by Mahatma Gandhi, with 300km Himalayan panoramas.
description: Kausani offers an unbroken 300 km wide vista of Trishul, Nanda Devi, and Panchachuli peaks. The sunrise and sunset golden glows on the snow crests are legendary.

name: Gangotri Dham
shortDesc: Sacred origin of River Bhagirathi and gateway to Gaumukh Glacier trek.
description: Nestled in pine and cedar forests along the foaming Bhagirathi river, Gangotri is dedicated to Goddess Ganga. The temple marks the spot where King Bhagirath meditated to bring Ganga to Earth.

name: Yamunotri Dham
shortDesc: Westernmost shrine of Char Dham and the source of River Yamuna.
description: Perched on the flanks of Bandarpoonch peak, Yamunotri honors Goddess Yamuna. Pilgrims trek 6 km from Janki Chatti and cook rice and potatoes in the boiling water springs of Surya Kund.

name: Tehri Lake & Water Sports
shortDesc: Massive emerald reservoir created by Tehri Dam, Asia's highest rockfill dam.
description: A rising water adventure hub offering jet skiing, banana boat rides, flyboarding, houseboat stays, and paragliding with panoramic views of the turquoise reservoir.
